messages:
rafael_cs: Heads-up — SparkChat (customer) reported that their invoice summarization bot started omitting entire line items after last night's model rollout. They say totals look right but individual items are missing. :frowning:

maya_support: Oof. Can you paste the customer's example and their prompt? also ask for prompt logs (request_id + model) if they have them.

rafael_cs: Pasted from customer (redacted):
```
PROMPT: "Summarize the invoice and list items in bullet points. Keep price and qty for each item."
INPUT: attached invoice image -> OCR -> extracted text (they provided OCR text)
CUSTOMER_OUTPUT_BEFORE_ROLLOUT: "- Widget A x2 $20\n- Service B x1 $100\nTotal: $140"
CUSTOMER_OUTPUT_AFTER_ROLLOUT: "Total: $140\nNotes: Payment received."
```
They also provided two request IDs: req_20260317_aa12 and req_20260317_bb07 (timestamps match the window).

jamie_ml: Thanks — can we confirm which model variant was rolled? deploy-bot, did the canary finish last night?

deploy-bot: rollout complete: redwood-serve/rw-infer-v3 -> traffic 100% @ 2026-03-17T03:12:10Z (canary -> prod). No rollback.

alex_runtime: Noted. Two quick hypotheses: 1) a decoding/stop-seq change that trims bulleted lists if prompt ends with "Summarize..." 2) a subtle instruction-following regression where the new model collapses repetition. Need the prompt logs including: model, temperature, max_tokens, stop sequences, and the raw prompt after template substitution.

maya_support: Reached out to SparkChat asking for the raw prompt they sent and the two request IDs logs (we asked them to export from their dashboard: prompt_log + model + response payload). Also asked for a minimal repro: run this exact text as plain input (no OCR) so we can isolate OCR pipeline vs model behavior.

rafael_cs: Customer replied with one of the request payloads for req_20260317_bb07: they included prompt payload: `{"input":"Summarize the invoice and list items in bullet points. Keep price and qty for each item.","model":"rw-infer-v3","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":250,"stop":["\n\n"]}` and returned text: "Total: $140\nNotes: Payment received." — so the model produced no bullets.

jamie_ml: Great, that rules out OCR pipeline for that request (since they provided the plain prompt). Can we reproduce locally? Rafael — can you run a quick curl against staging model pinned to older checkpoint (rw-infer-v2) and prod (rw-infer-v3) with exact payload? Put outputs in this thread. Use low temp.

rafael_cs: Running now. curl examples: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-infer-v2","input":"Summarize the invoice and list items in bullet points. Keep price and qty for each item.","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":250}'
```

rafael_cs: Results: rw-infer-v2 -> `- Widget A x2 $20\n- Service B x1 $100\nTotal: $140`

rafael_cs: Results: rw-infer-v3 -> `Total: $140\nNotes: Payment received.`

alex_runtime: Confirms regression between v2 and v3. Jamie — looks like a behavior change introduced during instruction tuning or RLHF. Can you run a quick eval on similar prompts across v2/v3 to see how widespread? Also check if stop tokens handling changed for trailing newlines.

jamie_ml: On it. I'll run batch of 120 prompts with variations (bullets requested, numbered list, explicit "Do not summarize: list items" etc). If it's systemic we'll tag as quality-regression and queue a rollback plan.

maya_support: For timeline/communications: requested customer minimal repro (they already gave plain prompt, so we can repro in prod). I told them we're investigating and asked if missing items cause production outage for them. They've said it's critical for invoice parsing — CSM escalation flagged.

jamie_ml: Early batch results: ~78% of prompts on rw-infer-v3 drop explicit bullet lists when customers ask for compact summaries, v2 preserved bullets ~92%. Looks like the new model favors short totals over enumerating items in some instruction contexts.

alex_runtime: We need quick mitigations: 1) revert traffic to rw-infer-v2 for the affected endpoint(s) (Customer-facing default model) until we have a fix, or 2) inject a temporary prompt patch that force-adds leading text "List each item explicitly:\n" before customer prompt via router. Which is faster?

jamie_ml: Revert is faster operationally. But if rollback not allowed for policy, prompt patch is quick stopgap. I can craft a conservative prompt patch that avoids changing semantics for other customers.

rafael_cs: @deploy-bot can we schedule a target rollback for the impacted model tag on the hosted API? If rollback requires approvals, escalate to eng leadership. Customer is waiting.

deploy-bot: rollback option: deploy rollback to rw-infer-v2 requires ops-approval. To request, run `/ops request-rollback rw-infer-v3 -> rw-infer-v2` in #eng-releases.

maya_support: I'll file the ops request and include the customer impact and batch results. Also sending customer a temporary workaround: prepend the text "PLEASE LIST EACH LINE ITEM SEPARATELY:\n" until we confirm rollout. Asked for permission to apply to their integration.

alex_runtime: Thanks. Jam: prioritize a narrow fix (instruction-following fine-tune or decoding tweak). Also check whether this intersects with recent stop-sequence improvements.

jamie_ml: Will follow up with a detailed root-cause and a plan in the thread when I have eval + diffs. For now, investigators: jamie_ml, alex_runtime, rafael_cs.

maya_support: Marking customer as P1 until rollback or prompt workaround in place. Keep me updated. :eyes:
